claim: MCP is presented as a plugin ecosystem for extending software, not as a replacement for tools or SDKs.
The speakers report that individual GitHub or HubSpot MCP definitions had consumed roughly 50,000 to 60,000 tokens.
note: Speaker report; catalog sizes were not independently measured.

claim: Adding an MCP that the builder does not control introduces an instruction and trust cost.
Tools needed by most users should be first class integrations rather than permanent long tail plugins.
A rise in use of a long tail MCP is a signal to migrate it into a supported integration.
MCP clients are most useful when end users have many capabilities the application builder did not anticipate.
